To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two zinc finger clusters of SIP1 and δEf1 bind independently to DNA and that the two CACCT and CACCTG sequences in the Xbra2, α4‐integrins and E‐cad genes are the optimal high‐affinity DNA binding sites for SIP1.

the δEF1 protein binds to two CACCTG sequences with two separated zinc finger clusters and that the integrity of both zinc finger clusters is essential for high‐affinity DNA binding and repressor activity of the δEF family.
the two zinc finger clusters of δEF1 bind to DNA as a pair of hands, and that SIP1 is a repressor of Xbra2 expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel DNA binding motifs and with the characterization of the molecular mechanisms of transcriptional regulation by the δEF1 and SIP1 proteins.
a new mode of DNA binding for multi‐zinc fingers.
the molecular mechanisms by which transcription factors regulate gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two zinc finger clusters of SIP1 and δEf1 bind independently to two target sequences, and that the two target sequences are located in a bipartite binding site.
δEF1 family proteins bind to DNA with two hands, one for each zinc finger cluster.

δEF1 family proteins bind with two hands (two zinc finger clusters) to two target sites (CACCT and CACCTG) and that the integrity of each zinc finger cluster is required for high‐affinity DNA binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the δEF1/SIP1 family of transcription factors bind with two hands, one for each target sequence.
δEF1 binds as a monomer to bipartite DNA sequences composed of two 5′‐CACC‐3′ motifs separated by 1 or 2 bp. The
δEF1 family proteins bind to bipartite elements in the promoter regions, with two separated zinc finger clusters contacting two target sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA binding of SIP1 and related δEF1 family proteins is a novel mode of DNA binding, in which two separated clusters of C2H2 zinc fingers contact two target sequences.
δEF1 family proteins bind to bipartite target sites, which may be a general mechanism for multi‐finger proteins to bind DNA.
the two CACCTG sites are required for the high‐efficacy binding of SIP1 and that both the zinc finger clusters of SIP1 are required for the binding of the protein to DNA and its repressive activity.
